name: North Adelaide
reason: Wikivoyage district with dining and heritage streets, but its sights (Montefiore Hill, St Peter's) are separate candidates; a suburb needs its own named sight.
objection: Wikivoyage gives North Adelaide its own section and visitors base there; a stroll through its streets is a half-hour+ visit.

name: Adelaide Park Lands
reason: Rule 1: experienceadelaide and Wikivoyage describe the Park Lands ring as a city feature; open park, walkable.
objection: A ring of ordinary city parks, and its notable parts (Botanic Garden, Himeji, Elder Park) overlap.

name: Bicentennial Conservatory
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage names it as 'a worthwhile place to visit' (tropical rainforest glasshouse, daily). Distinct attraction.
objection: Sits inside the Botanic Garden, so could be seen as part of a larger spot.

name: Rundle Lantern
reason: Rule 3: a lighting installation on a mall, minor, a few minutes' look.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it, and it is permanent nightly.

name: North Terrace
reason: Boulevard of museums; two counted sources, but the institutions are individual spots and the street adds a walk only.
objection: The street is the classic Adelaide cultural walk, named by two sources; but a duplicate of its institutions.

name: Migration Museum
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage See listing; a public museum with exhibits.
objection: One counted source only, small museum.

name: Tandanya National Aboriginal Cultural Institute
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage See listing; public Aboriginal art gallery.
objection: One source; modest visit.

name: State Library of South Australia
reason: Two tourism-board sources name it (heritage Mortlock reading room, free), but a library is a civic building by the rule.
objection: Rule 2 negative benchmark (Tūranga); the Mortlock Wing interior is a genuine heritage draw.

name: Adelaide Oval RoofClimb
reason: Operator/experience, not a place (COVERAGE: a spot is a place).
objection: Adelaide Oval itself is a place visitors tour, but that is a separate candidate.

name: Montefiore Hill
reason: Rule 1+3: Wikivoyage names it, the classic city lookout with Light's Vision statue.
objection: Short stop (about 15 min), but guide-named lookout.

name: St Peter's Cathedral
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage calls it one of Australia's most iconic churches, on postcards, free to enter, popular on city tours.
objection: A church; one source.

name: St Francis Xavier's Cathedral
reason: Wikivoyage lists it open daily, but the extract only says it is smaller than St Peter's; no named art or architecture to see.
objection: Open daily next to Victoria Square; cathedral architecture.

name: Australian Space Discovery Centre
reason: Wikivoyage lists a public space exhibit at Lot Fourteen; one source, short visit.
objection: Free public exhibit and distinct from other museums; one source and small.

name: Adelaide Holocaust Museum
reason: Wikivoyage lists it, but it opens only Sun and Tue-Thu, bookings required, small.
objection: Real museum, $10 entry; limited hours and one source.

name: Adelaide Casino
reason: Rule 2: a casino is a venue/business, not a sight.
objection: Housed in the heritage railway station.

name: Format Collective
reason: Small performance/zine venue; not a distinct visitor draw.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Government House, Adelaide
reason: Rule 2: vice-regal residence open only on set days; exterior only otherwise.
objection: Tourism board names it, open days exist.

name: Her Majesty's Theatre
reason: Performance venue, a building seen from the street; shows are events.
objection: Heritage theatre named in an itinerary.

name: Old Parliament House
reason: Museum of democracy, but no counted source found (southaustralia.com slug 404); Wikipedia only.
objection: Real museum open to the public; sources unverified.

name: Parliament House
reason: Tours offered but no counted source found; civic building.
objection: Tours exist, though the rule fails civic buildings.

name: Victoria Square
reason: Central square with the Three Rivers fountain; Wikivoyage mentions it only in history/transport, no See listing.
objection: Heart of the city grid; ten-minute look.

name: Chinatown, Adelaide
reason: Wikivoyage lists Chinatown as a pedestrian area (Moonta St) by the Central Market; a food strip, no thing to see.
objection: Named by a guide; essentially restaurants.

name: Ayers House
reason: Historic mansion museum (National Trust) open to the public; no counted source found.
objection: Genuine museum with tours; need a counted source.

name: Adelaide Festival Centre
reason: Performance venue; events, no standalone visitor draw.
objection: Riverbank landmark building.

name: Torrens Lake and Elder Park
reason: Riverbank park beside the Festival Centre; Wikivoyage mentions the Torrens only in passing; Popeye boats are an operator.
objection: Popular riverside promenade.

name: Adelaide Himeji Garden
reason: No counted source found; small garden in Park Lands (covered by the Park Lands).
objection: A genuine Japanese garden open daily.

name: Veale Gardens
reason: No counted source; ordinary Park Lands garden.
objection: Formal garden.

name: Botanic Park
reason: No counted source; Park Lands green beside the Zoo, weekly speakers' corner.
objection: Hosts WOMADelaide.

name: Rymill Park
reason: No counted source; ordinary Park Lands park.
objection: Lake and gardens.

name: Adelaide railway station
reason: Rule 2: working station, building seen from outside; the casino occupies it.
objection: Heritage building.

name: West Terrace Cemetery
reason: No counted source found; cemetery visited by guided tour only.
objection: Heritage tours exist.

name: Lot Fourteen
reason: duplicate of Australian Space Discovery Centre; precinct of offices.
objection: Precinct has public spaces.

name: JamFactory
reason: One tourism-board source (studio tours and gallery); it is a craft studio and shop.
objection: Public glassblowing tours and gallery vs shop/studio.

name: Carrick Hill
reason: Rule 1+2: southaustralia.com attraction page; 1930s house and gardens open to the public.
objection: Suburban location, limited days.

name: Beaumont House
reason: No counted source found; occasional events venue.
objection: Historic mansion.

name: Penfolds Magill Estate
reason: Tourism board source for the original Penfolds winery with city views, but it is a cellar door; brief holds the line unless a guide singles it out as a landmark estate.
objection: Penfolds' founding site (Grange); arguably a landmark estate.

name: Coopers Brewery
reason: Wikivoyage names the brewery visitor centre; a single famous brewery, but a business.
objection: Iconic Adelaide brand with a visitor centre vs a company site.

name: Burnside Village
reason: Shopping centre.
objection: Named by tourism board.

name: Melbourne Street
reason: Shopping/dining strip, no thing to see.
objection: Named by tourism board.

name: Unley
reason: Suburb of boutiques; no named sight.
objection: Tourism board gives it a page.

name: Capri Theatre
reason: Cinema venue; screenings.
objection: Wurlitzer organ is unusual.

name: Thebarton Theatre
reason: Concert venue; events.
objection: Historic theatre.

name: Piccadilly Cinema
reason: Cinema venue.
objection: Heritage cinema.

name: The Old Gum Tree
reason: Rule 3: minor memorial site (a plaque and stump area), no counted source.
objection: Historic proclamation site of South Australia.

name: Army Museum of South Australia
reason: Wikivoyage lists a military museum with limited hours (Sun, Mon, Wed); one source.
objection: Public museum; narrow hours and niche.

name: WOMADelaide
reason: Rule 4: annual festival.
objection: Famous festival.

name: National Pharmacies Christmas Pageant
reason: Rule 4: annual event.
objection: Iconic parade.

name: Gather Round
reason: Rule 4: annual sporting event.
objection: Major tourism draw.
